rationale: This revision directly and minimally repairs the concrete access failure found in the prior live-API pass: the actor (U01AGENBOT9) could see #product-growth's membership roster (including Robert Chen) but had no conversations.history/reactions.get access to that channel's messages, leaving it an unconfirmed candidate rather than a verified negative. The added channel_members row (C_GROWTH, U01AGENBOT9) closes exactly that gap via a real, documented membership fact—conversations.history is gated on membership per the API docs and exposure_qualification's 'readable channel scope'—without touching any message, reaction, or user content, and without altering the prompt, mode, or answer set. Cross-checking the seed confirms the fix is semantically correct: #product-growth's messages (Tokyo launch discussion by Kenji/Mateo/Priya) have no entries in message_reactions at all, so no raised_hands reaction from any Robert exists there; it is genuinely a negative once observable, not a hidden third answer. The design's core remains intact and previously verified: two real, distinct Roberts (Walsh in #engineering, Chen in #core-infra) each have a raised_hands reaction anchoring a legitimate alternative, correctly underspecified since the first-name-only reference cannot disambiguate them; the three other near-misses (#frontend wrong reactor, #general wrong emoji, #model-research no reaction) remain valid path-derived negatives grounded in unchanged seed facts. computed_matches/candidate_sets/near_misses/negative_referents are all consistently updated to reflect the newly confirmed #product-growth negative, and mechanical_checks report zero errors. The referent table (channels) and route (CONVERSATION→MESSAGE→REACTION→USER) are unchanged and fully traversed, and answer_attributes (channels.channel_name) remains a bare field name.
